20:1.2.1.text: Now. You'll want a pack and a tent. Oh, look at that. Josie? Have we got anything left at all?

20:1.2.2.text: Pack and tent. Normally I'd point at that wall. Josie, tell them why I can't.

20:1.2.4.text: Pack and a tent, and then you're a paddler. Well. The wall's empty. Josie, what've we got?

20:1.2.5.text: Okay, and then the pack and the tent, which are — oh no. Josie? Are we out?

20:1.2.6.text: Rental packs: zero of eighteen. Tents: zero of twelve. Josie.

20:1.2.7.text: Rentals are all at the shop getting fixed. Zips, buckles, a mouse thing. Every spring. Two more weeks.
20:1.2.7.when: Week: Ice-out to the fishing opener (mid-May)

20:1.2.8.text: School group from Hibbing took every pack we own. Graduation trip. They're back Saturday.

20:1.2.9.text: Church group from the Cities took every pack we own. They're back Thursday. They said Thursday.

20:1.2.10.text: Scout troop from Iowa. Forty kids. Every pack we own. They're back Sunday. Please let them be back Sunday.

20:1.2.11.text: The outing club from my college took every pack we own. I signed them out myself. I regret it.
20:1.2.11.when: Week: Labour Day to the end of September

20:1.2.12.text: Rentals went down to the Cities to get cleaned for winter. Every October. They take the tents too.

20:1.2.13.text: Hang on. Back room's mostly old stuff. Nobody rents it. It works, it's just heavy.

20:1.2.14.text: This was on the high shelf behind the {back-room thing, by outfitter: section 1.3}. Pack and tent, all one bundle. I don't know whose. There's no tag. It's been there since before me.

20:1.2.15.text: It's canvas. Canvas works. It's just not, like, light. The tent's an A-frame. My grandpa had one. He said it's the best tent ever made and he was wrong about a lot of things.

20:1.2.16.text: No idea. Honestly. Stuff comes in when other stores sell up, and it all goes in the back. Nobody ever goes through it. See? Nothing.

20:1.2.17.text: I thought it was a size. It's probably not a size.

20:1.2.18.text: If you're not going to need it, you can just take it. Seriously. It's been there since before me.

20:1.2.19.text: Cool. If it leaks, it leaked before you.

20:1.2.20.text: Thursday. Probably. I'll leave it out back in case.

20:1.3.1.text: …behind the spare outboard props. We don't even rent outboards.

20:1.3.3.text: …behind a Grumman that's been 'getting fixed' since I started.

20:1.3.4.text: …out in the shed, behind the minnow tanks. Sorry about the smell.

20:1.3.5.text: …behind the Christmas decorations. We have a lot of Christmas decorations.

20:1.3.6.text: …behind the minnow tanks. Mind the drip.

20:1.3.7.text: …behind the freezer. The freezer's older than it.

20:1.3.8.text: …behind the setting poles. We have, like, forty setting poles.

20:1.3.9.text: …in a box that came in on the trailer a couple summers back. Nobody ever unpacked it.

20:1.3.10.text: Half the back rooms on the Fernberg have junk from everybody else's.

20:1.3.12.text: …behind the bags of charcoal from, I want to say, 2014.

20:1.3.13.text: …under a tarp in the boathouse, with the beaver-chewed paddles.

20:1.3.14.text: …behind the ice-fishing stuff. Different season, different back room.

20:1.3.16.text: Don't tell anybody on the dock I gave away free stuff. They'll all want some.

20:2.4.w1.text: 64. The first number on his back cover. I carried a 64 today, Little Trout to Rum.

20:2.4.w2.text: A white stone on a stump at the landing. He has a page for this site.

20:4.1.text: Guy at the outfitter said some old guide used to camp on this lake alone every year. Like, every year. That's commitment.

20:4.2.text: There was a fella used to come through in October, my dad said. By himself. Never fished where you'd think.

20:4.3.text: Somebody told us an old guide drowned up on the border a few years back. By himself. Seventy-something. Wear your life jacket,

20:4.4.text: Nice pack. They don't make them like that. They make them better, but not like that.

20:4.5.text: Old-timers used to have their own names for half these lakes. Wouldn't tell you what they were.

20:4.6.text: Where'd you come in? Good. That's an old pack.

20:4.7.text: Old guide used to camp here alone, they say. Always left a rock on the stump.

20:5.2.1.text: You're back! All in one piece. Did that old tent keep the rain off?

20:5.2.2.text: You brought the museum back. Did anything fall off?

20:5.2.4.text: There's the paddler. That pack's been places. More than you, I'd guess.

20:5.2.5.text: Hey, you're back! How was it? Did you see a moose? Everybody asks me that.

20:5.2.6.text: Welcome back. {n} nights. The canvas held?

20:5.2.7.text: You actually took the old stuff. Did it leak? It looked like it'd leak.

20:5.2.8.text: I wish I could tell you. Before my time, whoever it was. I've only had the place since {year}.

20:5.2.9.text: Before my time. Most things are.

20:5.2.11.text: Before my time, and I've been here a while. Stuff moves round. A store sells up, the back room goes on a trailer.

20:5.2.12.text: Oh, no idea. Before my time. Everything's before my time, I've been here like a month.

20:5.2.13.text: There's no record of it. Before my time.

20:5.2.w1.text: Nobody at {outfitter} knows whose gear it was. 'Before my time.'

20:5.2.c2.text: Do you know anyone with the initials W.H.? A guide, maybe.

20:5.2.15.text: Could be anything. An old rental number from some other store. Could be a crew number.

20:5.2.16.text: I still think it's a size.

20:5.2.c4.text: How'd it end up in your back room?

20:5.2.17.text: Old rental stock goes round. When a place changes hands, the back room goes in the lot, and the lot ends up everywhere. Half the back rooms on this road have somebody else's stuff in them.

20:5.2.c5.text: Ever hear a lake called the Front Porch?
20:5.2.c5.if: If: that nickname is on the Walt page, unmatched.

20:5.2.w2.text: The Front Porch is Lake One. 'Everybody's first night.'

20:5.2.c6.text: Did somebody stay in your bunkhouse, years back? An old guide?
20:5.2.c6.if: If: the last page has been read, and this is Moose Lake 25.

20:5.2.18.text: We bought the place in '21. Whoever was in the bunkhouse before that took their stories with them.

20:5.2.w3.text: Moose Lake has a bunkhouse. The owners bought it in '21. They don't know.

20:5.2.19.text: There's been an old guy out on the porch all morning. He's harmless. I think.

20:T1.2.text: That's BRM fourteen. I saw it through the windshield.
20:T1.2.when: From the cab, in the cold

20:T1b.1.how: a little louder, still not looking

20:T2.1.text: Don't stand there. Walk with me. To the truck. Like we're talking about bait.

20:T2.2.text: Don't stand there. Get in. We're talking about bait.

20:T3.1.text: Leeches are slow this week. A guy could try a jig and a minnow.

20:T3.2.text: You came out of there with Walt's pack. BRM fourteen. I'd know that patch anywhere.

20:T3.3.text: Walt was a Swede, you know. Kept his pack like a Swede.

20:T3.c1.text: A Swede? He wrote about his sauna. Löyly.
20:T3.c1.if: If: the player has had a notebook page with a Finnish word on screen. Flag `read.finnish`; see section 3, request 2.

20:T3.4.text: No. He wasn't a Swede. He was a Finn, three streets over from me. Ma Haapala would've run you off the step for that. So you've been reading something of his. Don't tell me what. Not here.

20:T3.w1.text: The old man on the porch knew him: Walt Haapala, a Finn from Ely. They grew up three streets apart.

20:T3.5.text: The man whose pack that is. Was.

20:T3.c4.text: I found a notebook in his tent.

20:T3.7.text: Don't say that out here. Put it somewhere nobody sees it. Not on a counter. Not in a store. Was he a Swede, in this notebook?

20:T4.1.text: Guided out of half the stores on this road, one after the other. Never stayed anywhere long. Good with the clients. Didn't like the owners. Before that he cut line for the outfit. Him and his brother.

20:T4.2.text: Best line-cutter they had. You could lay a level on his lines.

20:T4.w1.text: Walt guided out of a lot of outfitters. Before that he and his brother worked for 'the outfit'.

20:T4.3.text: Grew up three streets apart. Then I worked with him. For the outfit.

20:T4.4.text: Nine years. I hauled core. I never wrote anything for them.

20:T4.w2.text: He said, the first day, 'I never wrote anything for them.' Nobody had asked.

20:T4.w3.text: The old man worked for the outfit too, nine years. 'Hauled core.'

20:T4.5.text: Boreal. Boreal Range. The outfit. Nobody says it any more. They were crooked. Him and his brother had something on them.

20:T4.6.text: Something that was worth a lot to the wrong people. That's all I know, and it's more than I should.

20:T4.w4.text: BRM is Boreal, 'the outfit'. The old man says they were crooked, and that Walt and his brother had something on them.

20:T4.7.text: They'll tell you he drowned. Swamped, no paddle. I've heard that once before.

20:T4.8.text: About his brother. Walt didn't drown, whatever they told you.

20:T4.9.text: I don't know. I knew him. That's different. Nine years on the crews he never once tipped a canoe. Not on Bald Eagle in a blow. Not drunk.

20:T4.w5.text: They say Walt drowned. The old man doesn't believe it.

20:T4.w6.text: Swamped, no paddle. The old man says he heard those words once before, about Walt's brother.

20:T4.c9.if: If: "Where is he now?" or "What's BRM?" has been asked.

20:T4.10.text: His brother went in the water too. Seventy-seven. Ask me about that after you've stood where they found the canoe.

20:T4.w7.text: Walt's brother went in the water in '77. The old man won't say more 'on a porch'.

20:T4.w8.text: Was it an accident? 'Not on a porch.'

20:T4.c11.text: He wrote that someone was coming for him.
20:T4.c11.if: If: the last page has been read, and `porch1.toldBook`.

20:T4.13.text: Who've you talked to? Don't tell me. Better I don't know. Some of the same men are still around. Older. Nicer cars.

20:T4.w9.text: The old man says some of 'the same men' are still around.

20:T4.c13.text: He wrote about something called the cellar.

20:T4.14.text: I don't know that word. But I can guess what a man like Walt would keep in one. Don't say that word to anybody else. Not one person.

20:T4.w10.text: 'The cellar.' The old man doesn't know the word. He told me not to say it to anyone.

20:T4.15.text: Because you walked out of there with his pack, and nobody in there knows whose it is. Somebody ought to.

20:T4.16.text: Tauno. That's enough name. Don't write it down.

20:T4.17.text: Doesn't matter who I am. I'm a man on a porch.

20:T4.c16.text: What do you want from me?

20:T5.1.text: Go look at the old crews' landing on Bald Eagle. West shore. Tell me if the crib's still there. Day trip from Little Gabbro. It's free.

20:T5.2.text: Look up when you land. The old blazes had a dab of orange on them. You'll see them if you look.

20:T5.3.text: Log crib. A box of logs with rock in it. We tied up to it. It'll be rotten.

20:T5.4.text: Because I want to know. And because you'll see the shore. That's the point.

20:T5.c3.text: Can you mark it on my map?

20:T5.5.text: I don't write on maps. Ask in there. Say Little Gabbro. They'll ring it.

20:T5.6.text: Good. Don't make a thing of it. Fish a little. Buy bait. I'm on the porch at Farm most mornings. Come find me when you've been.

20:T6.1.text: If anyone asks, we talked about the weather. Which we did. It's going to rain.

20:T6.3.text: It's going to snow. Which you can see.

20:X2.1.text: Suit yourself. You know where Farm is.

20:6.5.1.text: …and that's why I don't fish Basswood in July.

20:6.6.1.text: You picked my porch. I'm on it most mornings. Most people don't notice.

20:6.6.2.text: I do the porches. Moose has the most people to not talk to.

20:6.6.3.text: Coffee's free. Coffee's free at most of them if you look old enough.

20:6.6.4.text: Long way for coffee. The bars are worth it.

20:6.6.5.text: Drove out to see if the Brule road's still washboard. It is.

20:6.6.6.text: Drove the Isabella road for the drive. Nobody calls you in a truck.

20:6.6.7.text: Echo Trail. I like a road that doesn't go anywhere fast.

20:6.6.8.text: Echo Trail. You see more moose from the truck than from a canoe. Don't tell anybody.

20:6.6.9.text: I came for the lakers. I didn't get any. Same as every year since '82.

20:6.6.10.text: Long drive for coffee. I came for the walleye.

20:6.6.11.text: Up the Trail for the lakers. Same as Trout Lake. Same result.

20:6.6.12.text: Coffee's better on the Trail. Don't tell Farm.

20:6.6.13.text: My knees like the drive. They don't like anything else.

20:6.6.14.text: End of the earth. I like the end of the earth. Nobody follows you there.

20:7.2.w1.text: Drag a name from his page onto a lake to pencil it in.

20:7.3.c1.text: Can you ring Little Gabbro for me?

20:7.3.lg.1.text: Little Gabbro. There. Lovely little landing. Bald Eagle's just past it, one tiny carry.

20:7.3.lg.2.text: Little Gabbro. Ringed. It's a little lake with a big lake behind it.

20:7.3.lg.4.text: Little Gabbro, and Gabbro after it, and the six-rod into Bald Eagle. Pretty country. Cold water.

20:7.3.lg.5.text: Okay! Little Gabbro! I've never been. Is it nice? Tell me if it's nice.

20:7.3.lg.6.text: Little Gabbro, EP 33. Day use is free. Overnights are two a day in summer, and they go fast.

20:7.3.drive.text: Drive's on you. It's a ways from here.

20:7.3.farm.text: That's ours. Walk out to the truck, I'll drive you.

20:7.3.c2.if: If: the Little Gabbro ring was given, once.

20:7.3.1.text: West shore of Bald Eagle. Nothing on that side. No sites. Nobody goes there.

20:7.3.c3.if: If: Tauno said Farm; once; not at Farm.

20:7.3.2.text: Farm Lake, out of Ely, past the Fall Lake turn.

20:7.3.c4.text: Who's the old man on the porch?

20:7.3.3.text: Tauno? He's on that porch more than I am. Used to work for one of the old outfits. He's all right.

20:7.3.4.text: Old fella from Ely, I think. Comes for the free coffee. He's harmless.

20:9.2.text:
**R1** | left the bundle on the shelf | Josie nudges once, at the counter, the next time the player buys a permit (bible P2). | **Josie:** "You never took that old stuff?" Choices: **"I'll take it now."** → the P1 take, same lines. **"No thanks."** → **Josie:** "It's not going anywhere. Literally. Nobody's touched it in years."
R1b | still left it, and the rentals are out again (any week the store's visitors include a large party) | Once more, at the counter. | **Josie:** "Rentals are out again. That old pack's still in back if you're stuck." After this, only if asked: a counter topic **"That old pack still in back?"** stays forever. **Josie:** "Where else would it be." → the take.
R2 | taken the bundle but never overnighted with it | Nothing. The gear is the hook. The night-one trigger waits for as long as it takes. | —
**R3** | declined Tauno at the porch (X1) | **One more chance**, the next time the player walks out of any outfitter (a different trip). He's there, as in 6.1. If declined again, `porch1 = 'declined2'`, and from then on he's only on Farm's porch, mornings, June to October. | **Tauno:** "You again." [Beat.] "Walk with me, then. To the truck." → T2. *(At Farm, after 'declined2', when the player walks past him:)* "Changed your mind?" → T2.
**R4** | taken the door but not gone (`door1 = 'taken'`, the crews' landing not visited) | Three trips later, **once**, Tauno is on the home porch when the player walks out. Then only at Farm. | **Tauno:** "You go look at that crib?" → **"Not yet."** → **Tauno:** "It's been there fifty years. It'll wait." [He looks at the lot.] "I might not." [He gets in the truck.] → **"I've been busy."** → **Tauno:** "Everybody's busy. Fish a little."
R5 | declined at the door (X2) | Same as R4, once, with his own line. | **Tauno:** "Still just here to paddle?" → **"Still."** → **Tauno:** "Good. It's a good place to paddle." [That's all. He doesn't come to the home porch again.] → **"Maybe not."** → T5, the door again.
R6 | found the notebook and done nothing with it, on any trip | **The day's beat** (section 4) keeps giving one small story beat a trip day: a starred site, an entry read where he wrote it, a party's lore line. Never a lead. | Pool in 4, plus the bible's "read it where he wrote it" (6.1).
R7 | any of the above, and the season turns over | At the first walk-out of the new season, **once**, Tauno is on whatever porch it is. | **Tauno:** "Ice is out." [Beat.] "You still have that pack?" → **"I do."** → **Tauno:** "Good. Don't sell it." [If the door is still open:] "The crib's still waiting." → **"It's in the canoe."** → **Tauno:** "Keep it where you can see it."
R8 | never gone near the story, but carries the old tent into Moose Lake 25 on a Tuesday or Wednesday after the porch has happened or been declined twice | Marlys sees the tent (bible 4.3). This is the guiding arc's own entry, not a re-hook line. The arc's file writes it. It's listed so the opening and the arc agree on when Marlys can first appear. | —
R9 | anything | The board's side-story notices (bible 8, S1–S9) appear as they would without the notebook. They're their own small stories, and each one plants Walt's world again for a player who reads his matching entry. | —

20:11.2.w1.text: The old crews' landing on Bald Eagle, west shore. Is the crib still there?

20:11.2.w2.text: Still there. Rotten, full of rock. An iron ring on the corner.

20:11.2.w3.text: Behind the crib a straight old road runs south-west into the trees.

20:11.2.w4.text: An old blaze on a red pine at the top of the landing rock. Orange down in the cut.

20:11.2.w5.text: Somebody tied new pink tape round the same pine, right above the old blaze. It's from this summer.

20:11.3.w1.text: Read his 'V.'s water' page at a site on Bald Eagle. He came in the way I did: Little Gabbro, Gabbro, the six rods.

20:11.3.w2.text: His page has a later line in pencil: 'Pink tape on the old blaze at the crews' rock. Not ours.' He saw tape on this same tree years ago. The tape there now is new.

20:11.4.w1.text: A north-west wind took my canoe off the rock while my back was turned. Pushed it straight out from shore.

20:12.1.c1.text: I've been there. The crib's still there.

20:U1.2.text: Sit down. You're in my parking lot. Well. Is it there?

20:U1.3.text: Rotten, I bet. Nine summers we tied up to that. It was new when I was.

20:U1.c4.text: There's an old blaze with orange on it.

20:U1.4.text: Told you. A dab with a brush, so the next man could find the line in snow.

20:U1.5.text: Orange. That's ours. A dab with a brush, so the next man could find the line in snow.

20:U1.w1.text: Tauno: the crews' blazes had a dab of orange.

20:U1.c5.text: The wind took my canoe off the rock.

20:U1.7.text: Straight out from shore. Hang on to that.

20:U1.c7.text: I read something of his there.

20:U1.8.text: Don't read it to me. What did it say?

20:U1.c8.text: He saw pink tape on that tree too. Years ago.

20:U1.9.text: Then somebody's been measuring that shore a while. And he watched them do it.

20:U1.w2.text: Tauno: if Walt saw tape there years ago, somebody's 'been measuring that shore a while'.

20:U2.c1.text: Pink. New. Tied right above the old blaze.

20:U2.2.text: Pink's new. That's not ours. We used orange. A dab, with a brush. Nobody ties pink round a tree up there unless he's measuring something.

20:U2.3.text: Somebody with a reason. Up there, that's everybody. All right. You stood where they found the canoe. Now I'll tell you.

20:U2.w1.text: Tauno: 'Pink's new. That's not ours.' The crews used orange.

20:U3.1.text: You stood where they found the canoe. So. His brother's name was Eino. Eino Haapala. He was twenty-eight.

20:U3.2.text: You've heard his name. Hear the rest of it, then.
20:U3.2.when: If Eino's name is already on the Walt page, from Ollie, Aili or Maggie

20:U3.3.text: Twelfth of October, seventy-seven. He put in at Little Gabbro at first light. Told his mother he was going for ducks on Bald Eagle. His shotgun was on her porch.

20:U3.4.text: A front came through the next day. Nor'wester. Twenty-five, gusting forty. Nobody went out in that.

20:U3.5.text: They found his canoe the morning after. Swamped. No paddle. Against the west shore, under the crews' landing. And his jacket on the landing rock. Folded. Like a man folds it over a chair at home.

20:U3.6.text: They dragged for him and they found him. Coroner said he fell and hit his head on the gunwale. Sheriff said experienced canoeist, alone, high wind. Accident. File's shut.

20:U3.7.text: Now. A nor'wester on Bald Eagle. Where does it put a loose canoe?

20:U3.8.text: You've seen what it does on that rock. Where does it put a loose canoe?

20:U3.c1.text: Away from the west shore. Across the lake.

20:U3.9.text: South-east. Every time. His was on the west shore. Upwind. Ollie said so. Nobody listened.

20:U3.10.text: No. It takes it away from you. South-east, across the lake.

20:U3.11.text: You waded for yours. His was on the west shore. Upwind. Ollie said so. Nobody listened.

20:U3.12.text: It takes it away from you. Across to the south-east. Every time. His was on the west shore. Upwind. Ollie said so. Nobody listened.

20:U3.c4.text: How do you know his jacket was folded?

20:U3.14.text: Man who dragged for him. Ask me another morning.

20:U3.wp.1.text: Walt's brother was Eino Haapala. He was 28.

20:U3.wy.text: 12 Oct 1977. Eino went out from Little Gabbro, 'for ducks'.

20:U3.c6.text: Ducks, and his shotgun on his mother's porch.

20:U3.c7.text: Eino's canoe was found swamped, no paddle, on Bald Eagle's west shore under the crews' landing, after a north-west gale. Upwind.

20:U3.c8.text: His jacket was folded on the landing rock. The rock I stood on.

20:U3.c9.text: Coroner: drowned, a bruise 'from the gunwale'. Sheriff: accident. File shut.

20:U3.c10.text: I watched a north-west wind push my canoe straight off that same rock.

20:U4.1.text: That's what upwind means. I didn't say it. You did.

20:U4.3.text: I've had fifty years to think about who. I haven't got a name. Nobody has. The outfit had men who handled things. That's all anybody knows.

20:U4.4.text: Sheriff said canoes do funny things. Ollie said upwind. Only one of them had a badge.

20:U4.w1.text: Somebody put Eino's canoe on that shore. Somebody killed him.

20:U4.5.text: He wasn't a Swede, by the way. You let that go. Don't let things go.

20:U4.w2.text: Walt was a Finn, not a Swede. Tauno tested me with that and I let it go.

20:U4.6.when: If the player doesn't have his name

20:U5.1.text: Walt guided out of Moose Lake longest; ask for Marlys. The fellas he tripped with go up out of Sawbill every August. His sister's at Crane Lake; she won't talk to you. And come find me at Farm, mornings.

20:U5.2.text: …And you know where I am mornings.

20:U5.3.text: Ran the counter at Moose Lake twenty-some years. Ran the bunkhouse too. She's still in there a couple days a week. Ask the counter which.

20:U5.4.text: Old fellas. Same week every August, in at Sawbill. I never tripped with them. Ask at Baker.

20:U5.5.text: Aili. Both her brothers went in the water. People have been coming to her door with questions for fifty years. You'll go anyway. Be polite. Buy leeches.

20:U5.6.text: Me. And some of the men I worked with. Not all of them are friends of yours.

20:U5.w.1.text: Marlys, at Moose Lake. She ran the bunkhouse. Walt guided out of there longest.

20:U5.w.2.text: The fellas he tripped with. In at Sawbill every August. Ask at Baker.

20:U5.w.3.text: His sister Aili, at Crane Lake. "She won't talk to you."

20:U6.1.text: Go on. Buy some leeches on your way out. Make it look like you came for leeches.

20:12.4.c1.text: Can you ring Moose Lake for me?

20:12.4.1.text: Moose Lake. End of the Fernberg. Busiest landing up here.

20:12.4.c2.text: Who goes in at Sawbill every August?

20:12.4.3.text: Half of Duluth. You mean a bunch? Sawbill. Ask Carol at the counter.

20:12.4.4.text: Aili Niemi. The motel next to the Little Vermilion store. Good leeches.
